changes.basis: TIME, 2023: held to the 'standards of engineering rigor that apply to a bridge', 'the entire field would be shut down tomorrow'. 'We are not prepared.' He wants a halt, which goes beyond a safety case.
TIME, 2023: the moratorium 'needs to be indefinite and worldwide'; 'Make immediate multinational agreements to prevent the prohibited activities from moving elsewhere.' Far beyond existing law.
TIME, 2023: solving safety 'could very reasonably take at least half that long' (half of 60 years), and still: 'Shut it all down.' He accepts any delay.
TIME, 2023: 'preventing AI extinction scenarios is considered a priority above preventing a full nuclear exchange'. No lab-scale gamble is acceptable to him.
TIME, 2023: 'Shut down all the large training runs.' And: 'Shut it all down. We are not ready.'
TIME, 2023: 'anyone talking of arms races is a fool'. AGI Ruin, 2022: a careful lab that holds back only lets another 'destroy the world two years later'.

AGI Ruin, 2022: 'We've got no idea what's actually going on inside the giant inscrutable matrices and tensors of floating-point numbers' (§25). Interpretability cannot yet tell whether a system is planning to kill us.
AGI Ruin, 2022: 'Fast capability gains seem likely, and may break lots of previous alignment-required invariants simultaneously.' A premise he has held since the 2008 AI-Foom debate.
AGI Ruin, 2022: stopping one lab still leaves 'some eager open-source collaborative from destroying the world a year later'. No direct statement on open weights was opened, hence medium.
Techno-Optimist Manifesto, 2023: 'any deceleration of AI will cost lives. Deaths that were preventable by the AI that was prevented from existing is a form of murder.'
Why AI Will Save the World, 2023: 'Open source AI should be allowed to freely proliferate'; 'There should be no regulatory barriers to open source whatsoever.'
Lex Fridman #407, 2023: 'the market is much more efficient at achieving this sort of reliability optimum than sort of heavy-handed regulations that are written by the incumbents'.
Lex Fridman #407, 2023: 'I don't think stagnation or slowing down is actually an option.' e/acc notes, 2022: 'You cannot stop the acceleration'.
TIME, 2024: 'the future has to be open source, if nothing else, for reasons of cultural diversity, democracy, diversity'.
TIME, 2024: that an intelligent system 'wants to take control' is 'just completely false'. X, 21 Apr 2026: 'I didn't say p(doom) was zero'; 'All estimates are pulled out of thin air'.
ABC, 14 Sep 2026: Amodei's call to slow AI development is 'very sensible'. Not a full stop, though: 'I don't think we should stop developing it altogether.'
Ai4, Aug 2026: open weights make it 'so easy for people to take these big foundation models' and 'train them to do bad things like cyber attacks'. He adds: 'that battle's been lost'.

Co-authored paper, 2024: 'developers of frontier AI should carry the burden of proof to demonstrate that their plans keep risks within acceptable limits'. ABC, 2026, reports he wants pre-release testing.
80,000 Hours, Apr 2026: 'even a 1% chance of something going really, really bad is not acceptable to me'.
Blog, 11 Sep 2026: 'This suggests pacing the advances: not training or deploying AIs without a strong safety case' that convinces independent experts.
June 2026: 'It is time to go beyond transparency to more serious and binding regulation of AI'; government 'should have the power to block or deter deployment' of risky models.
Senate, 2023: 'third-party testing, a new national agency, and an international coordinating body, all of which I support'; 'systems that break the rules must be removed from the market'.
Diary of a CEO, Dec 2025: 'prove to us that the risk is less than one in 100 million per year of extinction or loss of control'. A 1% risk is a million times over that bar.
Substack, 13 Sep 2026, on Trump's claim that whoever wins AI wins: 'I continue to oppose this zero-sum thinking'.
Substack, 13 Sep 2026: AI is 'not going to cure cancer either, at least not anytime soon or on its own'. He files 'hyperbolic cheer' under hype, so delay costs little.
Doom Debates, Nov 2025: with 'nothing like the FDA for AI', 'it's definitely over 90% that we lose control'. Loss of control, not fraud or job loss, is the harm he expects.
Guardian, May 2025: firms 'need to also calculate the Compton constant, the probability that we will lose control over it'. Compton's bar for the Trinity test was about one in three million.
Aug 2026 update, his own section: 'things are roughly on track for AI 2027, just going a bit slower'; 'I increase the speed of post-AC takeoff'. His ASI median there: March 2029.
Plan A (co-author), July 2026: 'they delay the creation of superintelligence to 2040'; 'It's what we think should happen, not what will happen'. The benefits are deferred on purpose.
AI 2027 (lead author), 2025: 'the impact of superhuman AI over the next decade will be enormous, exceeding that of the Industrial Revolution'. His worry is takeover, not scams.
Right to Warn letter (signatory), 2024: 'many of the risks we are concerned about are not yet regulated'. Also signed the 2025 Global Call for AI Red Lines; Plan A needs new treaties.
Plan A summary (co-author), 2026: 'Track down the world's AI-relevant compute'; 'Resume R&D under safety-case-based regulation'. A regime rather than a licence in name, hence medium.
Plan A (co-author), 2026, is a joint deal: 'an international coalition to delay the development of superintelligence'. The go-it-alone pacing case is his colleagues' post, not his.
Plan A summary (co-author), 2026: 'Companies must argue that capability improvements involve very low risk before proceeding.'
Plan A (co-author), July 2026: 'they delay the creation of superintelligence to 2040. It would have happened much sooner (in 2030, to be precise)'. A decade's delay, as a recommendation.
Situational Awareness, 2024: 'I'm most worried about things just being totally crazy around superintelligence, including things like novel WMDs, destructive wars, and unknown unknowns.'
Essay, July 2026: 'advances on the frontier are outpacing our understanding of the technology'; we need 'time and space' and 'we aren't doing that'. Proposes a new standards body.
TechPolicy.Press, 2025: the work 'hidden behind the facade of artificial intelligence' is sold as automated 'when it's always people'. Co-author Hanna: AI 'will make your job shittier'.
